quotes.text: Setup Intents set up payment credentials but don’t process payments.
Both Payment Intents and Setup Intents go through the same set of states.
In that case, attempting to capture the funds moves it to `processing` or `succeeded` depending on the payment method.
However, cancellation might fail due to a limited and varying cancellation time window.
A SetupIntent with a `succeeded` status means that the setup is successful.

old_evidence.text: Other payment methods, such as cards, are processed more quickly and don’t go into the `processing` status.
You can cancel a SetupIntent at any point before it’s in a `processing` or `succeeded` state.

answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paymentintents/lifecycle distinguishes a merchant's attempt to collect payment through a PaymentIntent from saving credentials without charge through a SetupIntent. New raw lines 13-35 and old raw lines 10-86 describe attaching a payment method, confirming when the customer supplies details, and handling additional customer action such as 3DS when required. Attachment and confirmation are commonly combined. Asynchronous payment methods can remain processing, while a separately authorized PaymentIntent can require capture and then enter processing or succeed. PaymentIntent success completes the payment flow, while SetupIntent success permits attaching the method to a Customer for future use. Failure returns either object to requires_payment_method. Neither lifecycle describes cancellation at succeeded. A PaymentIntent can be canceled before processing or succeeded, with a limited and varying processing exception for ACH, ACSS, AU BECS, BACS, NZ BECS and SEPA. Cancellation irreversibly invalidates future attempts and releases held PaymentIntent funds. Too many PaymentIntent confirmations can also trigger cancellation. A SetupIntent can be canceled before processing or succeeded, and cancellation irreversibly invalidates future setup attempts. Its lifecycle describes no processing exception or held-fund release. source-stripe-payment-intents.md distinguishes creation, verified server fulfillment, SetupIntent reuse and deferred Charge data, and routes Checkout Session-bound cancellation to the separate API authority, but its generic cancellation paragraph should explicitly scope the two Intent types. The guide's Checkout Sessions recommendation is scoped to most integrations, with Session-specific client confirmation in its elements examples.
